text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Editorial: President Tudjman has built himself a firm position of a "stability factor" in the region. Announced visits of his German and French counterparts only serve to confirm this.
- Health minister Andrija Hebrang says women will be given mandatory 72 hours to consider their decision on abortion under the new law.
- Ivan Penic, the current privatisation minister to replace interior minister Ivan Jarnjak.
- A man cannot divorce a pregnant woman and divorce is also banned for parents with children under one year of age, according to a draft family law.

- American paper USA Today in its special November supplement, in which Croatian companies and state institutions paid $500,000 for advertisements, places Croatia on the Baltic Sea and claims 96 percent of the population speak Serbo-Croatian.
- Some 9,000 rail workers may have to be laid off in an effort to rescue the ailing company HZ.

- Interior minister Ivan Jarnjak, who resigned two days ago for apparent failure to stop protests against attempts to close down an independent radio, was offered a head post at the Office for National Security.
- Owners of nationalised property will receive 20-year bonds, repayable from year 2000 as compensation. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
